title: Red Planet Detective
tagline: Where did Mars's water — and its air — go?
briefing: Ancient rivers left their traces on Mars. Your job is to find where the water went and measure the atmosphere still escaping into space. A low orbit lets radar and cameras map the surface. Add an ultraviolet spectrograph to observe escaping hydrogen from a distance, or pick an elliptical orbit to sample the upper atmosphere directly. You have $800 million to cover the science, spacecraft and launch.

objectives.name: Monitor global dust & clouds
objectives.blurb: Daily weather maps to track dust storms.

objectives.name: Measure atmospheric escape
objectives.blurb: Sample escaping gases directly or track the hydrogen corona in ultraviolet.

objectives.name: Map buried ice
objectives.blurb: Find water ice under the surface — future astronauts will need it.

objectives.name: Image landing sites in high resolution
objectives.blurb: Metre-scale images to certify safe landing zones.

objectives.name: Find water-altered minerals
objectives.blurb: Clays and salts that only form in liquid water.

notes: NASA MAVEN demonstrated UV imaging of escaping hydrogen. For this objective, UV observations and direct atmospheric sampling are alternate ways to earn credit. The volume requirements and low-orbit science yield are gameplay assumptions.

title: Giant's Heart
briefing: Jupiter formed early, and its deep atmosphere may preserve clues about how the planets grew. Send an orbiter to measure water, map the magnetic field and weigh the interior. At Jupiter, sunlight is roughly one twenty-seventh as strong as at Earth, and trapped radiation threatens your electronics. Choose a route that leaves room for the power and shielding your science needs.

objectives.name: Measure deep-atmosphere water
objectives.blurb: How much water formed Jupiter? The answer tells us how the solar system was built.

objectives.name: Weigh the core
objectives.blurb: Map the gravity field to find out whether Jupiter has a solid core.

objectives.name: Map the magnetic dynamo
objectives.blurb: The strongest planetary magnetic field — where is it generated?

objectives.name: Explore the polar auroras
objectives.blurb: Auroras bigger than Earth, powered by the magnetosphere.

objectives.name: Share the view
objectives.blurb: Colour images of the poles for scientists and the public.

title: Lunar Ice Prospector
tagline: Is there water in the Moon's eternal shadows?
briefing: Sunlight never reaches the floor of some craters near the Moon’s poles. Lunar Prospector found extra hydrogen there, evidence that ice could be present. Your mission is to check where cold traps and hydrogen-rich areas overlap. Your starter spacecraft already carries a neutron detector and a thermal instrument. For a short first flight, keep those instruments and take the direct lunar rideshare. At the debrief, look for the two measurements you returned and the objectives that would need extra instruments.

objectives.name: Map polar hydrogen
objectives.blurb: Hydrogen in the soil is the fingerprint of buried ice.

objectives.name: Take the temperature of cold traps
objectives.blurb: Is it cold enough in the shadows for ice to survive?

objectives.name: Map polar topography
objectives.blurb: 3-D maps to find where shadows are permanent.

objectives.name: Spot surface frost
objectives.blurb: Look for the spectral signature of exposed ice.
